merger_description:
DB Grid 1 Pty Ltd as trustee for DB Grid AU Bid Trust, a special purpose vehicle which is an indirect subsidiary of DigitalBridge Partners III, LP, proposes to acquire 100% of the contestable smart metering division of PLUS ES by way of a sale by the vendors of their interests in the partner entities that form PLUS ES (being 5 unit trusts and their respective corporate trustee companies) pursuant to a Securities Sale and Purchase Deed (the **Acquisition**).

DigitalBridge Partners III, LP is an investment fund managed by an affiliate of DigitalBridge Group, Inc.

DigitalBridge is a dedicated, global-scale digital infrastructure investment company headquartered in Florida, United States, that primarily invests, directly and through its managed funds and their portfolio companies, in 5 key areas: data centres, cell towers, fibre networks, small cell; and edge infrastructure.

PLUS ES is an Australian metering business that is owned by a partnership between the NSW Government, a consortium of IFM Investors, APG Asset Management and AustralianSuper.

PLUS ES is a group of entities which is comprised of the following divisions:

* the contestable smart metering division which delivers contestable smart metering services to retailers
* the regulated metering division which delivers regulated electricity metering services for networks; and
* the infrastructure services division which provides community battery energy storage systems, electrical vehicle charging infrastructure and infrastructure services to commercial customers.

The Acquisition will only include the contestable smart metering division, with the regulated metering and infrastructure services divisions to be transferred out of PLUS ES via a restructure prior to completion of the Acquisition.

Relevantly, PLUS ES is an Australian Metering Services Provider operating across the east coast of Australia that co-ordinates all metering services for smart meters, including provision, installation, maintenance, data collection and data delivery. PLUS ES provides Metering Co-ordinator, Metering Provider and Metering Data Provider services to residential customers and commercial and industrial operators, including energy retailers, embedded network operators and energy network businesses. PLUS ES provides these services under end-to-end service agreements with energy retailers.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationships
between DigitalBridge or its controlled portfolio companies
and PLUS ES in the supply of smart metering services in
Australia.
b. there is no horizontal overlap between Softbank or its
controlled portfolio companies and PLUS ES in the supply of
smart metering services in Australia.
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-Softbank’s
acquisition of DigitalBridge.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
